title: Prefill Orbital Scheduler: clock sync and kernel steering for mixed-MIG fleets
creator: Samira Patel
description:
Problem: Mixed-MIG GPU fleets (H100 / L40S / A10 partitions) see variable prefill latency and unstable attention kernel selection when clock governors differ across slices. This causes tail-latency spikes for short-chat workloads and increases cost due to suboptimal microkernel choices.

Goal: Implement an "Orbital Scheduler" that coordinates lightweight clock reconciliation, kernel steering hints, and prefill window sizing per-MIG-slice to stabilize kernel choice and reduce prefill tail by 20-35% without increasing average power. The scheduler should run in the serving runtime and emit telemetry for kernel candidate ranking, thermal headroom, and prefill window hit rates.

Scope: H100 + L40S + A10 mixed fleets, focus on prefill->decode transition paths and attention microkernels. Deliverables: runtime patch with scheduler, new telemetry metrics, an experiment harness for fleet A/B, documentation for ops config knobs (clock_tolerance_ms, pref_window_ms, kernel_prio_bias).

Non-goals: full hardware-level clock control (we will use existing clock governance APIs), changes to customer-facing API, or model-level quantization changes.

Success metrics: 25% reduction in 99th prefill latency on targeted workloads, 10% fewer kernel fallback events, no customer-visible QoS regressions in production canary cluster.
comments: 2026-02-20 Samira Patel: Created ticket. Initial notes from infra sync: mixed-MIG customers reported tail latency for short prompts. Attached profiling snapshot in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/MIG+prefill+profiling (draft).

2026-02-26 Liam O'Connor: PoC design completed. Orbital Scheduler idea: periodic lightweight probe that samples token-density histogram and slice clocks, assigns a per-request kernel hint and prefill window. Probe runs at 1s cadence by default. Trade-offs discussed: probe frequency vs noise; decided to start with conservative 1s and expose config.

2026-03-02 Samira Patel: Lab experiments (h100-l40s-a10 mixed rack) show kernel choice stabilized when prefill window >= 60ms and when clock_tolerance_ms <= 20ms. Observed 18% drop in 99th prefill latency for chat-short workload. Link to notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/Prefill-Orbital-Experiments
2026-03-07 Infra review: Security OK (no new surface), ops requested a metric for 'orbital_probe_failures' and 'kernel_hint_mismatch' for alerting. Added to telemetry plan.

2026-03-10 Liam O'Connor: Implemented runtime prototype: scheduler threads per-GPU host aggregate per-slice clock and microkernel score. Introduced a lightweight arbitration that prefers microkernels with lower variability under current clock headroom. Benchmarks: p99 prefill improved further to ~27% on synthetic traces. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4281

2026-03-14 Samira Patel: Rolling canary to staging fleet tomorrow. Plan: 2% traffic canary for 24h, monitor metrics: prefill_p99, kernel_fallback_rate, orbital_probe_failures, gpu_power_variance. If any regression >5% on p50 latency or increased fallback rate >3pp, abort and revert.
notes: Design trade-offs: we prefer runtime-side heuristics to avoid touching scheduler firmware. This keeps rollout fast but accepts some jitter with aggressive EDF-style packing.
Implementation detail: kernel_hint is encoded as an enum string sent to the microkernel selector; implementation uses existing kernel scoring table with additional clock_variability_penalty.
Telemetry: new metrics will be tagged by sku and mig_slice_id; dashboards will live in Grafana folder 'runtime/prefill/orbital'.
